newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Cocoa seen forging ahead, still bullish.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Cocoa seen forging ahead, still bullish.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
LIFFE cocoa futures are more likely to forge ahead than pull back as the current chart picture remains bullish, technical analysts said on Thursday.
However, traders called the market to open five stg down after a $22-$33 a tonne loss in New York on Wednesday.
Elli Gifford, an independent technical analyst, put support at Tuesday's low of 1,097 stg basis September.
An immediate resistance is pegged at 1,120, followed by 1,165 and 1,270.
"If above 1,120, the market will form a flag," she said.
Flag is short-term chart formation that develops over a two to three-week period and is generally accepted as being continuation pattern. In an upward trending market, the flag slopes downward.
"Basically, it is a bullish picture and I suspect the recent downward reaction is all over."
"On balance, the market is likely to go firm rather than seeing any further weakness," she said.
Broker GNI said in a commentary that London would really need to drop below 1,097 to cause any real concern, and below 1,065 to negate the bullish move.
In fundamental news, Ecuadorean cocoa exports could suffer from heavy rains which have hit the country's main plantations, industry officials said.
"If this El Nino current phenomenum continues, producing heavy rains, then damage to the Christmas crop is expected," National Cocoa Exporters Association president Jose Carvajal told Reuters.
Continuing rain could cause fungus outbreaks, he said.
The El Nino pattern of warm ocean temperatures occurs every two to seven years with profound effects on global weather. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
